name: Biology Foundation Models
blurb: AlphaFold, protein language models and the models that predict how molecules behave.
title: Biology Foundation Models
answer: Biology foundation models learn the rules of proteins, DNA and small molecules from very large datasets, the way language models learn text. AlphaFold 2 made accurate protein structure prediction routine in 2021, AlphaFold 3 extended it to interactions with DNA, RNA and drug-like molecules in 2024, and protein language models capture evolutionary information without labelled data.

reading.body:
Biology foundation models turn protein, DNA and small molecule prediction into a commodity input, so the advantage shifts to proprietary experimental data.

The pattern is a two step progression. AlphaFold 2, published in 2021, made accurate protein structure prediction routine for most proteins. AlphaFold 3, released in May 2024 by Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs, extended the same approach to nucleic acids, small molecules and their interactions. Protein language models sit alongside these, capturing evolutionary information without labelled data.

For AI specifically, the constraint this data implies is not modelling capacity but data ownership. Once structure prediction is available to everyone, a research team's edge comes from the experimental results it can fine tune on for its own targets. That is a data problem, not a compute problem, and the data given here does not quantify either side of it.

What the data does not cover is scale. It names no parameter counts, no training compute, no dataset sizes, and no cost figures, so it cannot support any claim about how much compute these models consume or how that demand interacts with power and buildings. It also stops at 2024 and lists no results beyond the two AlphaFold releases.

sections.body: Structure prediction is now a commodity input. The advantage lies in proprietary experimental data that fine tunes these models for your targets.
